lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I missed that tooth. I'm not missing the next one.
lines.script: [wistful, admitting] I missed that TOOTH. [resolved, quiet] I'm not missing the NEXT one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's TNB. "Babe. Come home. Your house. NOW. It's about Bready Mercury."
lines.script: [reading, puzzled] It's TNB. [reading aloud, urgent] "Babe. Come home. Your house. NOW. It's about Bready Mercury."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Also there are acorns in the flour."
lines.script: [reading, baffled] "Also there are ACORNS in the flour."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hi, babe. I missed you. Now please don't panic, but look at the island.
lines.script: [tender, quick] Hi, babe. I missed you. [calm, bracing him] Now please don't panic, but look at the ISLAND.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The jar is gone! Where's Bready Mercury?
lines.script: [alarmed] The jar is GONE! [frantic] Where's Bready Mercury?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I fed him at eight and sang him his song. Then I went out for grape soda, and when I came back the window was open and he was gone.
lines.script: [recounting, calm] I fed him at eight and sang him his song. [sheepish] Then I went out for grape soda, [bewildered] and when I came back the window was open and he was GONE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Which song did you sing him?
lines.script: [curious, serious] Which song did you sing him?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: "I Want to Bake Free."
lines.script: [straight-faced] "I Want to... [punchline] Bake FREE."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And now he HAS!
lines.script: [punchline, delighted] And now he HAS!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He had help, babe. Four toes in front and five in back. I looked it up. Those are squirrel feet.
lines.script: [informing, calm] He had help, babe. [precise, proud] Four toes in front and five in back. I looked it up. [grave] Those are SQUIRREL feet.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A squirrel took our starter? He's nine years old! He's flown Delta One twice!
lines.script: [outraged, disbelief] A SQUIRREL took our starter? [punchline, indignant] He's nine years old! He's flown Delta One TWICE!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And it left this. I've seen every horror movie ever made, babe, and this is how they all start.
lines.script: [ominous, hushed] And it left THIS. [resigned, nonchalant] I've seen every horror movie ever made, babe, [grave, matter-of-fact] and this is how they ALL start.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The window was open, so it isn't breaking and entering. It's baking and entering.
lines.script: [reasoning, lawyerly] The window was open, so it isn't breaking and entering. [punchline, proud] It's BAKING and entering.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Don't make me laugh. This is all very jarring.
lines.script: [stifled, anxious] Don't make me laugh. [punchline, strained] This is all very JARRING.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe! That's seven! Amy texted me about the other six. I've never been so proud.
lines.script: [thrilled] Babe! That's SEVEN! [fond, amused] Amy texted me about the other six. [melting, proud] I've never been so PROUD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I have news from Long Island too. It happened at Amy's school. A kickball and a sneaker are frozen in an orange block as big as a washing machine, and it's hanging in the air over second base.
lines.script: [sober, reporting] I have news from Long Island too. It happened at Amy's school. [amazed, precise] A kickball and a sneaker are frozen in an orange block as big as a washing machine, [disbelief] and it's HANGING in the air over second base.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That makes five. And every one is bigger than the last. Babe, what comes after a washing machine?
lines.script: [counting, uneasy] That makes FIVE. [ominous] And every one is bigger than the last. [dread, quiet] Babe, what comes after a WASHING MACHINE?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don't know. I just don't want to find out in my kitchen.
lines.script: [admitting, small] I don't know. [firm, anxious] I just don't want to find out in my KITCHEN.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And nobody goes anywhere alone. So we get him back together.
lines.script: [firm, protective] And nobody goes anywhere ALONE. [warm, resolved] So we get him back TOGETHER.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Together. Hold on, Bready Mercury. We're coming!
lines.script: [resolved] Together. [calling out, heroic] Hold on, Bready Mercury. We're COMING!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A peanut triangle! What does it mean?
lines.script: [astonished] A peanut TRIANGLE! [pleading, curious] What does it mean?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nothing good, babe. In the movies a triangle never means anything good.
lines.script: [grim, nonchalant] Nothing good, babe. [dry, knowing] In the movies a triangle NEVER means anything good.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They took something of ours too. Bready Mercury is gone, jar and all.
lines.script: [hurt, realizing] They took something of OURS too. [aggrieved] Bready Mercury is gone, jar and all.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Your bread jar? Oh, Tom. I'm so sorry.
lines.script: [confused, sympathetic] Your bread jar? [soft, sincere] Oh, Tom. I'm so SORRY.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: She also says there was a big flash in the park on Sunday morning. She wrote down the time.
lines.script: [relaying, hushed] She also says there was a big FLASH in the park on Sunday morning. [wide-eyed, matter-of-fact] She wrote down the TIME.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A flash! TNB, did you hear that?
lines.script: [alarmed] A FLASH! [turning, urgent] TNB, did you hear that?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I heard it, babe. I was hoping I didn't.
lines.script: [grim, resigned] I heard it, babe. [wry, defeated] I was HOPING I didn't.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Olivia said you saw a flash on Sunday.
lines.script: [careful, curious] Olivia said you saw a flash on SUNDAY.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Sunday, 6:12 in the morning, at the picnic tables. One flash and no thunder. By 6:20 the squirrels had lookouts. Come and see what it left.
lines.script: [crisp, official] Sunday, 6:12 in the morning, at the picnic tables. [hushed, grave] One flash and no thunder. By 6:20 the squirrels had LOOKOUTS. [beckoning, grim] Come and see what it left.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The whole picnic is grey! And there's an orange block on the table. It's as big as a bathtub!
lines.script: [stunned] The whole picnic is GREY! [alarmed] And there's an orange block on the table. [disbelief] It's as big as a BATHTUB!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, there's a picnic basket inside it. And a squirrel! He's halfway into the basket with his tail in the air!
lines.script: [hushed, amazed] Babe, there's a picnic basket inside it. [gasping] And a SQUIRREL! [incredulous, delighted] He's halfway into the basket with his tail in the AIR!

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Caught in the act. I've wanted to see that for nineteen years. I didn't want to see it like THIS.
lines.script: [grim, vindicated] Caught in the act. [wistful, clipped] I've wanted to see that for NINETEEN years. [pained, flat] I didn't want to see it like THIS.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's never had one hold still before. She doesn't know what to do with it.
lines.script: [amused, fond] She's never had one hold STILL before. [wry] She doesn't know what to do with it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, Mr. Squirrel. Are you all right in there?
lines.script: [polite, concerned] Excuse me, Mr. Squirrel. [gentle, earnest] Are you all right in THERE?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. I know this part now. There's going to be a little round hole in the side. There it is.
lines.script: [settling in, calm] Okay. I know this part now. [knowing] There's going to be a little round hole in the side. [pleased, grim] There it IS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You know the signs!
lines.script: [impressed, delighted] You know the SIGNS!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I learned from the best. And there's going to be a burnt flashbulb. I just can't find it.
lines.script: [smug, fond] I learned from the BEST. [investigating] And there's going to be a burnt flashbulb. [puzzled] I just can't find it.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Are you looking for this? I found it under the last table at 6:31. Bagged, labeled and dated. Exhibit A.
lines.script: [smug, officious] Are you looking for THIS? [crisp, proud] I found it under the last table at 6:31. [deadpan, grand] Bagged, labeled and dated. Exhibit A.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the sixth one! Could we have it? My mother keeps them in a drawer.
lines.script: [thrilled] That's the SIXTH one! [hopeful, polite] Could we have it? [earnest, helpful] My mother keeps them in a DRAWER.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: It's evidence. Your mother can file a request.
lines.script: [flat, officious] It's EVIDENCE. [prim, dry] Your mother can file a REQUEST.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Whose picnic was it?
lines.script: [curious] Whose picnic was it?

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: A birthday party, setting up early. They ran when the squirrels got big. The cake is still on table two. Nobody touch the cake. The cake is also evidence.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] A birthday party, setting up early. They ran when the squirrels got BIG. [grave, pointed] The cake is still on table two. [stern, deadpan] Nobody touch the cake. The cake is also EVIDENCE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dragonfly, lemon, fish, hat, kickball, and now a whole picnic basket. This is the biggest one yet, and it's five blocks from my house.
lines.script: [tallying, rapid] Dragonfly, lemon, fish, hat, kickball, and now a whole picnic basket. [alarmed] This is the BIGGEST one yet, [anxious, small] and it's five blocks from my HOUSE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: One thing at a time, babe. That block isn't going anywhere. Bready Mercury already did.
lines.script: [soothing, calm] One thing at a time, babe. That block isn't going anywhere. [punchline, dry] Bready Mercury already DID.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That peanut is as big as a trash can, and it's booing us!
lines.script: [amazed] That peanut is as big as a TRASH CAN, [incredulous] and it's BOOING us!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...I looked anyway.
lines.script: [sheepish, admitting] ...I looked ANYWAY.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tough crowd. Don't worry, babe. They'll come out of their shell.
lines.script: [sympathetic, dry] Tough crowd. Don't worry, babe. [punchline, playful] They'll come out of their SHELL.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Who's the Chairman?
lines.script: [curious, polite] Who's the CHAIRMAN?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, Mr. Twig. We're looking for a jar of sourdough starter. He answers to Bready Mercury.
lines.script: [polite, formal] Excuse me, Mr. Twig. [earnest] We're looking for a jar of sourdough starter. [proud, fond] He answers to Bready Mercury.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: I've never heard of Operation Big Bread.
lines.script: [stiff, evasive] I've NEVER heard of... [flustered, quick] Operation Big Bread.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. He just told us the name of the operation.
lines.script: [incredulous, delighted] Babe. He just told us the name of the OPERATION.

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmf mmf. (And nobody touches Agent Crumb. He's on a mission.)
lines.script: [muffled, fierce] Mmf mmf. [muffled, proud] (And nobody touches Agent Crumb. He's on a MISSION.)

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Is Agent Crumb the one in the basket?
lines.script: [curious, polite] Is Agent Crumb the one in the BASKET?

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmf. (Three days in there. Bravest squirrel we have.)
lines.script: [muffled, solemn] Mmf. [muffled, reverent] (Three days in there. Bravest squirrel we HAVE.)

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm wearing most of the sandbox, babe.
lines.script: [deadpan, patient] I'm wearing most of the SANDBOX, babe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It suits you. You've always looked good in earth tones.
lines.script: [warm, sincere] It suits you. [punchline, playful] You've always looked good in EARTH tones.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A little yellow toy truck. That's Lachlan's.
lines.script: [fond, proud] A little yellow toy truck. [warm, certain] That's LACHLAN'S.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I always keep a heel of sourdough in my jacket for emergencies. Nara, this is an emergency.
lines.script: [proud, matter-of-fact] I always keep a heel of sourdough in my jacket for EMERGENCIES. [grave, firm] Nara, this is an emergency.

lines.speaker: Tiny voice
lines.text: Password accepted. Welcome, Agent...
lines.script: [tiny, formal] Password accepted. Welcome, Agent...

lines.speaker: Tiny voice
lines.text: ...wait. You're very tall. Are you a squirrel?
lines.script: [puzzled, tiny] ...wait. You're very TALL. [suspicious, squeaky] Are you a squirrel?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know! I feel terrible. I'm going to apologize as soon as we get up there.
lines.script: [guilty, anguished] I know! I feel TERRIBLE. [resolved, earnest] I'm going to apologize as soon as we get up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She smells bread! Bready Mercury is up at the top of this tree, and there's no ladder.
lines.script: [excited] She smells BREAD! [realizing, anxious] Bready Mercury is up at the top of this tree, [dismayed] and there's no LADDER.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: HANG IN THERE, BREADY! WE KNEAD YOU!
lines.script: [bellowing, heroic] HANG IN THERE, BREADY! [punchline, booming] WE KNEAD YOU!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Was that "need" with a K?
lines.script: [puzzled, curious] Was that "need" with a K?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's always with a K, babe.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, proud] It's ALWAYS with a K, babe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's an X on every porch on 2nd Avenue. And there's a drawing of Nara. It says "THREAT LEVEL: VERY HIGH."
lines.script: [reading, stunned] There's an X on every porch on 2nd Avenue. [amazed] And there's a drawing of NARA. [reading aloud, solemn] It says "THREAT LEVEL: VERY HIGH."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She likes it. They got her good side.
lines.script: [amused, fond] She likes it. [proud, dry] They got her good SIDE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It says "OPERATION BIG BREAD" across the top. Everything connects to the jar, babe. That's how corkboards work.
lines.script: [reading aloud, hushed] It says "OPERATION BIG BREAD" across the top. [knowing] Everything connects to the jar, babe. [dry, delighted] That's how corkboards WORK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "BY ORDER OF THE CHAIRMAN. WINTER IS COMING. HOARD EVERYTHING."
lines.script: [reading aloud, grave] "BY ORDER OF THE CHAIRMAN. [ominous] WINTER IS COMING. HOARD EVERYTHING."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And look in the corner. It's the picnic table, with a sad face drawn on it. "AGENT CRUMB. STILL IN THE ORANGE THING. DAY THREE."
lines.script: [hushed, gentle] And look in the corner. It's the picnic table, with a sad face drawn on it. [reading aloud, somber] "AGENT CRUMB. STILL IN THE ORANGE THING. [grave] DAY THREE."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They can't get him out either.
lines.script: [quiet, sympathetic] They can't get him out EITHER.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: "SUPPLY LINE. ROPE LADDER. SEE BUCKET, PANTRY." Babe, that's our way up.
lines.script: [reading aloud, brisk] "SUPPLY LINE. ROPE LADDER. SEE BUCKET, PANTRY." [excited] Babe, that's our way UP.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She really pulled her weight.
lines.script: [punchline, proud] She really pulled her WEIGHT.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: All forty pounds of it.
lines.script: [deadpan, fond] All FORTY pounds of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That squirrel is as big as a mailbox, and he's wearing a TIE!
lines.script: [awestruck] That squirrel is as big as a MAILBOX, [incredulous, delighted] and he's wearing a TIE!

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: On Sunday there was a flash at the picnic tables. It took my best agent, and it made me big enough to run things. So I'm running things.
lines.script: [grim, pompous] On Sunday there was a flash at the picnic tables. [aching, small] It took my best agent, [grandiose, defiant] and it made me big enough to run things. So I'm RUNNING things.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sir, at the door I told one of your squirrels that I was a squirrel. That wasn't true, and I'm sorry.
lines.script: [formal, humble] Sir, at the door I told one of your squirrels that I was a SQUIRREL. [guilty, earnest] That wasn't true, [sincere] and I'm SORRY.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Apology noted. You're still trespassing.
lines.script: [stiff, grudging] Apology noted. [pompous, firm] You're still TRESPASSING.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's eight! Babe, you're on a roll.
lines.script: [delighted] That's EIGHT! [fond, proud] Babe, you're on a ROLL.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And look at the bottom of the jar. Something gold is stuck to it.
lines.script: [noticing, curious] And look at the bottom of the jar. [intrigued] Something GOLD is stuck to it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's a gold coin with a picnic basket on it! He climbed out of the jar again and glued it on.
lines.script: [amazed] It's a gold coin with a picnic basket on it! [exasperated, fond] He climbed out of the jar AGAIN [punchline, amused] and glued it on.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: I found that under the picnic table on Sunday. It's the shiniest thing I own, so I kept it under the best thing I own.
lines.script: [proud, wistful] I found that under the picnic table on Sunday. [grand, earnest] It's the SHINIEST thing I own, [tender, simple] so I kept it under the best thing I own.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara! That's not bread! It only smells like bread!
lines.script: [alarmed] Nara! That's not BREAD! [pleading] It only SMELLS like bread!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Let her carry it, babe. She's wanted a gold frisbee since the lemon.
lines.script: [easy, soothing] Let her carry it, babe. [fond, amused] She's wanted a gold FRISBEE since the lemon.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: The dog has my coin. ...Fine. I'm practicing sharing. I'll walk you out. It's procedure.
lines.script: [stunned, flat] The dog has my coin. ...Fine. [stiff, dignified] I'm practicing SHARING. I'll walk you out. It's PROCEDURE.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: That coin is MINE. I'm following that dog.
lines.script: [outraged, shrill] That coin is MINE. [stubborn, sputtering] I'm following that DOG.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Agent Crumb. Bravest squirrel I ever commanded. He went in for one sandwich.
lines.script: [hushed, grieving] Agent Crumb. Bravest squirrel I ever COMMANDED. [aching, small] He went in for one SANDWICH.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: That's MY coin, and that's MY agent in there. I want them both back.
lines.script: [indignant, shrill] That's MY coin, [aching, demanding] and that's MY agent in there. I want them both BACK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm sorry about your friend, sir.
lines.script: [quiet, sincere] I'm sorry about your FRIEND, sir.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara, I've told you. We don't play fetch with gold.
lines.script: [gentle, correcting] Nara, I've told you. [firm, fond] We don't play fetch with GOLD.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She only eats bread if you throw it, babe. And that coin smells like Bready Mercury.
lines.script: [reasoning, easy] She only eats bread if you THROW it, babe. [amused, coaxing] And that coin smells like Bready Mercury.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...One throw. A very small one.
lines.script: [giving in, sheepish] ...One throw. A very SMALL one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It rolled into the little round hole. TNB, it fits! It fits exactly!
lines.script: [stunned, hushed] It rolled into the little round HOLE. [wonder, rising] TNB, it fits! It fits EXACTLY!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. It's cracking.
lines.script: [awed, hushed] Babe. It's CRACKING.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: AGENT CRUMB! You're out! By order of the Chairman, I hereby declare this the greatest day in the history of...
lines.script: [ecstatic, shouting] AGENT CRUMB! You're OUT! [pompous, grandiose] By order of the Chairman, I hereby declare this the GREATEST day in the history of...

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Squeak.
lines.script: [tiny, startled] Squeak.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The grass is green. The tables are brown. Babe, it all came back.
lines.script: [awed, quiet] The grass is green. The tables are brown. [overwhelmed] Babe, it all came BACK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And the Chairman is just a squirrel. Sir? Mr. Chairman?
lines.script: [gentle, stunned] And the Chairman is just a SQUIRREL. [tentative, hopeful] Sir? Mr. Chairman?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He can't talk anymore.
lines.script: [quiet, sad] He can't talk ANYMORE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He still knows where your back fence is. Saturdays, babe. A deal is a deal.
lines.script: [gentle, wry] He still knows where your back fence is. [warm, firm] Saturdays, babe. A deal is a DEAL.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: But what just HAPPENED?
lines.script: [reeling, wild] But what just HAPPENED?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The coin has a picnic basket on it, and the block had a picnic basket in it. That hole is exactly as big as a coin.
lines.script: [reasoning, slow] The coin has a picnic basket on it, and the block had a picnic basket IN it. [realizing, dawning] That hole is exactly as big as a COIN.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB, the coin came OUT of that hole. Nara just put it back!
lines.script: [breathless, realizing] TNB, the coin came OUT of that hole. [amazed, rising] Nara just put it BACK!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: So the block breaks, the color comes back, and the squirrels go back to being squirrels. Babe. It's a key.
lines.script: [reasoning, rapid] So the block breaks, the color comes back, and the squirrels go back to being squirrels. [hushed, thrilled] Babe. It's a KEY.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Nineteen years I've watched this park, and I've never seen anything like that. What did you DO?
lines.script: [stunned, indignant] Nineteen years I've watched this park, and I've never seen anything like THAT. [demanding, shrill] What did you DO?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The dog did it.
lines.script: [simple, proud] The DOG did it.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Then the dog is going in the report.
lines.script: [crisp, officious] Then the dog is going in the REPORT.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. I have a coin with a lemon on it in my pocket.
lines.script: [quiet, realizing] TNB. [dawning, intense] I have a coin with a LEMON on it in my pocket.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And I have a hat.
lines.script: [dazed, quiet] And I have a HAT.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose has the dragonfly. My father has the fish. Amy has the kickball.
lines.script: [tallying, quick] Rose has the DRAGONFLY. My father has the FISH. [amazed] Amy has the KICKBALL.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Five blocks and five coins. Babe, we've been carrying the answer around like loose change.
lines.script: [stunned, dry] Five blocks and five coins. [punchline, wry] Babe, we've been carrying the answer around like LOOSE CHANGE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara, you're a genius. You're getting so much chicken.
lines.script: [proud, doting] Nara, you're a GENIUS. [promising, delighted] You're getting SO much chicken.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...I'm sorry. I think that one is used up.
lines.script: [gently, apologetic] ...I'm sorry. [kind, sad] I think that one is used UP.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We owe her a throw, babe.
lines.script: [soft, fond] We owe her a THROW, babe.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Evidence released. Tell your mother to keep it somewhere dry.
lines.script: [formal, grand] Evidence RELEASED. [prim, officious] Tell your mother to keep it somewhere DRY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: First Bready Mercury goes home. Then the lemon, then the hat. And then I'm calling my mother.
lines.script: [resolved, planning] First Bready Mercury goes home. Then the lemon, then the hat. [determined] And then I'm calling my MOTHER.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Also in the report: the squirrels are regular squirrels again, and a dog fixed my park.
lines.script: [officious, crisp] Also in the report: the squirrels are regular squirrels again, [grudging, dry] and a DOG fixed my park.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold ball. Nara, THIS gold we can throw!
lines.script: [delighted] A gold ball. [announcing, thrilled] Nara, THIS gold we can THROW!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Finally! She's been waiting since the lemon.
lines.script: [relieved, fond] FINALLY! She's been waiting since the LEMON.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Before you put him back, I have something. I was saving it for when you landed. Then the squirrels happened.
lines.script: [tender, shy] Before you put him back, I have something. [gentle] I was saving it for when you landed. [punchline, wry] Then the squirrels HAPPENED.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He kept climbing out of the jar, so I made him a bigger home. I threw it on the wheel last week. It came out of the kiln on Thursday.
lines.script: [explaining, shy] He kept climbing out of the jar, so I made him a bigger HOME. [proud, quiet] I threw it on the wheel last week. [soft, bright] It came out of the kiln on THURSDAY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You made him a crock! It has his name on it. And a crown!
lines.script: [overjoyed] You made him a CROCK! [amazed, delighted] It has his name on it. And a CROWN!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He's a Queen fan, babe. He needs a crown.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, fond] He's a Queen fan, babe. [punchline, dry] He needs a CROWN.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's perfect. ...It came out on Thursday? I was at conference night. I love watching you open the kiln.
lines.script: [overwhelmed, soft] It's PERFECT. [realizing, wistful] ...It came out on Thursday? I was at conference night. [admitting, tender] I love watching you open the KILN.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I know. I almost waited.
lines.script: [gentle, rueful] I know. I almost WAITED.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Don't wait for me. Just save me the next one.
lines.script: [warm, generous] Don't wait for me. [tender, hopeful] Just save me the NEXT one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: There. Now he's got room to rise to the occasion.
lines.script: [satisfied, easy] There. [punchline, playful] Now he's got room to RISE to the occasion.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nuts! I've been waiting all day for you to say it.
lines.script: [delighted] NUTS! [thrilled, teasing] I've been waiting ALL DAY for you to say it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I was saving it for the end. Tell Amy to put me down for one.
lines.script: [smug, easy] I was saving it for the END. [playful, fond] Tell Amy to put me down for ONE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was completely nuts. And I wouldn't have missed it.
lines.script: [contented, warm] It was completely NUTS. [sincere, soft] And I wouldn't have missed it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This coin has flown nine thousand nine hundred miles in my pocket, and it never earned one SkyMile.
lines.script: [proud, precise] This coin has flown nine thousand nine hundred miles in my pocket, [punchline, aggrieved] and it never earned one SKYMILE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Then give it somewhere to land, babe.
lines.script: [gentle, wry] Then give it somewhere to LAND, babe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It worked! It worked on purpose!
lines.script: [ecstatic] It WORKED! [disbelief, thrilled] It worked on PURPOSE!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look at her face. That dog has no zest for it at all.
lines.script: [amused, observing] Look at her face. [punchline, deadpan] That dog has no ZEST for it at all.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He's a hill again. Goodnight, sir. I'm still coming up for a nap on Sunday.
lines.script: [soft, fond] He's a hill again. Goodnight, sir. [gentle, wry] I'm still coming up for a NAP on Sunday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He liked the naps.
lines.script: [quiet, tender] He liked the NAPS.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I know. That's why I'm going.
lines.script: [soft, simple] I know. That's why I'm GOING.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My first award. I've had it for nine days.
lines.script: [wistful, fond] My first award. [dry, proud] I've had it for NINE days.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You don't have to use it. We could look for another way.
lines.script: [gentle, concerned] You don't have to use it. [offering] We could look for another way.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. There's a hat stuck in a block, and I'm wardrobe. It was an honor just to be nominated.
lines.script: [easy, loving] Babe. There's a hat stuck in a block, and I'm WARDROBE. [punchline, mock-solemn] It was an honor just to be NOMINATED.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And THAT is why you put the table back.
lines.script: [triumphant, smug] And THAT is why you put the table BACK.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Great take.
lines.script: [satisfied] Great take.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You just gave away the only award you ever won.
lines.script: [moved, amazed] You just gave away the only award you EVER won.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I've still got the gold steamer. And I've got a babe who flew out to watch me work. I'm still on a streak.
lines.script: [easy, content] I've still got the gold steamer. [tender, teasing] And I've got a babe who flew out to watch me work. [punchline, smug] I'm still on a STREAK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My favorite son! Did you eat?
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, delighted] My favorite SON! [warm Long Island accent, bossy] Did you EAT?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, get everybody. Rose's coin, Dad's coin and Amy's coin. I know what they're for!
lines.script: [urgent, breathless] Mom, get everybody. Rose's coin, Dad's coin and Amy's coin. [triumphant] I know what they're FOR!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Slow down. You sound like your father with a fish.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, firm] Slow down. [warm Long Island accent, punchline, dry] You sound like your father with a FISH.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every coin goes back into the little round hole in its own block. The block breaks, the color comes back, and everything that woke up goes back to normal. Nara figured it out.
lines.script: [explaining, rapid] Every coin goes back into the little round hole in its own block. [excited] The block breaks, the color comes back, and everything that woke up goes back to normal. [proud, fond] Nara figured it OUT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The round hole is where the coin came OUT! Tata, I drew that hole on every single page!
lines.script: [bursting, triumphant] The round hole is where the coin came OUT! [indignant, proud] Tata, I drew that hole on every single PAGE!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then we're going to the pond. All of us, together. Amy, hold the phone up so your brother can see.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, commanding] Then we're going to the pond. All of us, TOGETHER. [warm Long Island accent, bossy] Amy, hold the phone up so your brother can SEE.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: But it's my treasure.
lines.script: [pouting, small] But it's my TREASURE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Cozy Rosie, that dragonfly has been stuck in there a long time.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, gentle] Cozy Rosie, that dragonfly has been stuck in there a long TIME.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...Okay. Fly, bug.
lines.script: [sniffling, giving in] ...Okay. Fly, BUG.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's a GUMBALL MACHINE! You put the coin in and the bug comes out!
lines.script: [shrieking, thrilled] It's a GUMBALL MACHINE! [excited, explaining] You put the coin in and the bug comes OUT!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's not how gumball machines work.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, prim] That's NOT how gumball machines work.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It is NOW.
lines.script: [defiant, bright] It is NOW.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I saw it! Amy, hold the phone still!
lines.script: [thrilled] I SAW it! [pleading, quick] Amy, hold the phone STILL!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I AM holding it still. Rose is jumping.
lines.script: [brisk, exasperated] I AM holding it still. [dry] Rose is JUMPING.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Gold like my teeth. Best thing I ever caught.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, bragging] Gold like my TEETH. [thick New York accent, fond] Best thing I ever caught.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, you have to put it in.
lines.script: [insisting, bright] Boppy, you HAVE to put it in.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Have to? I WANT to. Gold is for keeping. Fish are for jumping.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, defensive] Have to? I WANT to. [thick New York accent, punchline, proud] Gold is for keeping. Fish are for JUMPING.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...He was a small one anyway.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, rueful] ...He was a small one ANYWAY.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You gave away your gold, hubby.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, amused] You gave away your GOLD, hubby.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I've got plenty left.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, smug] I've got PLENTY left.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I paid for those.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, punchline, dry] I PAID for those.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: My one gold star.
lines.script: [wistful, quiet] My one gold STAR.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mom, you give out forty of those a week.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, precise] Mom, you give out FORTY of those a week.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I give them out. Nobody ever gave ME one.
lines.script: [dry] I give them OUT. [wry, wistful] Nobody ever gave ME one.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...Moss needs his shoe.
lines.script: [softening, resolved] ...Moss needs his SHOE.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Monday morning just got a lot easier to explain.
lines.script: [relieved, brisk] Monday morning just got a lot easier to EXPLAIN.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Amy! Put me down for nine today. And put Tom down for eight.
lines.script: [cheerful, teasing] Amy! Put me down for NINE today. [playful] And put Tom down for EIGHT.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nine? I'm not counting yours. You're a professional.
lines.script: [incredulous, brisk] Nine? I'm not counting YOURS. [dry, punchline] You're a PROFESSIONAL.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's all six. Tata, I need a bigger chart.
lines.script: [satisfied, brisk] That's all SIX. [bossy, matter-of-fact] Tata, I need a bigger CHART.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Good. Now who is DOING this? Somebody is going around with a flashbulb.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, firm] Good. [warm Long Island accent, suspicious] Now who is DOING this? Somebody is going around with a flashbulb.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don't know yet, Mom. I have three more bulbs for your drawer.
lines.script: [admitting, honest] I don't know yet, Mom. [helpful, earnest] I have three more bulbs for your DRAWER.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The drawer is ready.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk] The DRAWER is ready.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, one more thing. The library is WHISPERING. Like actually. Page says it's fine. It's NOT fine. Come home.
lines.script: [urgent, hushed] Tata, one more thing. The library is WHISPERING. [insisting] Like actually. Page says it's fine. [alarmed, bossy] It's NOT fine. Come home.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They did all three, and I watched it on a phone.
lines.script: [amazed, quiet] They did all three, [wistful, rueful] and I watched it on a PHONE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Then go and watch the next one in person. I'll feed Bready. Fifty and fifty, and I'll sing.
lines.script: [tender, firm] Then go and watch the next one in PERSON. [easy, fond] I'll feed Bready. Fifty and fifty, and I'll sing.
